question: Which galaxy is the nearest to the Milky Way?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Andromeda Galaxy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andromeda Galaxy** is the nearest spiral galaxy to the Milky Way.
 
• It is located approximately **2.537 million light-years** from the Milky Way.
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy is also known as **Messier 31** or **M31**.
 
• It is on a collision course with the Milky Way, and the two galaxies are expected to merge in about **4.5 billion years**.
 
• Andromeda Galaxy is visible to the naked eye in the night sky under good conditions and is one of the brightest Messier objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Milky Way** and the Andromeda Galaxy are part of the **Local Group** of galaxies, which contains more than 54 galaxies.
 
• The **Triangulum Galaxy** (M33) is also part of the Local Group and is the third-largest galaxy in the group.
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy has a diameter of about **220,000 light-years**, making it the largest galaxy in the Local Group.
 
• It contains approximately **one trillion stars**, which is more than twice the number of stars in the Milky Way.
 
• The Andromeda Galaxy has a number of satellite galaxies, including M32 and M110.
